spec_match.rationale: The model mirrors ParseDeclarativePerformanceObserverPolicy exactly: report-to accepted only as a string item, entry-types only as an inner list of tokens/strings filtered through the four-value vocabulary, include-user-timing only as an inner list keeping string items, capture-early-failures only as a boolean item, unknown keys ignored, and any RFC 8941 dictionary violation voiding the whole header. All nine cases from declarative_performance_observer_parser_unittest.cc are embedded verbatim as the expected contract and reproduce 9/9 both in Node and in the browser (verified via DOM dump).

interactive.rationale: Free-form textarea parses on every keystroke into a rejected/parsed verdict, the exact policy JSON, and per-directive drop notes; nine preset buttons load the edge cases; the run-all button replays Chromium's unit tests with a per-test pass/fail table (screenshot verified: 9/9, green verdict, policy JSON rendered).

blurb_alignment.rationale: Blurb promises malformed/mistyped/unknown-token inputs through a faithful re-implementation pinned against the real unit tests; the page delivers exactly the nine contracts plus extra void cases (trailing comma, uppercase key).

edge_cases.rationale: The page IS the edge-case demo: whole-header-void vs silently-dropped is the central distinction, including implicit-true bare keys, non-list entry-types, token-vs-string allowlist items, type mismatches, unknown directives, and the empty-header-empty-policy case. The honesty note names the one thing it cannot be: the browser's own network stack.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/6594955352080384, RFC 8941's dictionary-parsing section, and the explainer syntax anchor.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables throughout; preset buttons invert the global button colours and set both background and color in both states; verdict banners use accent-emerald/accent-rose left borders on bg-paper; the suite table scrolls in its own wrapper.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Desktop verified at 1280 (screenshot read). An initial true-360px measurement found real horizontal overflow (scrollWidth 599) from long unbroken inline code such as the Chromium file path; fixed with overflow-wrap:anywhere on inline code and re-measured clean (scrollWidth 345 == clientWidth) with a 360-wide screenshot read. Buttons/textarea meet 44px targets. No physical touch device was available.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive form controls panel no horizontal overflow mobile
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Long unbreakable strings (paths, identifiers) need overflow-wrap; wide tables belong in their own scroll container.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied after measurement caught the overflow: main p/li code gets overflow-wrap:anywhere, the unit-test table scrolls inside .suite-wrap, and the policy pre uses pre-wrap with break-word.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible live region status readout for asynchronous state changes
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Parse results and suite outcomes should be announced via live regions and rendered as real table semantics.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The verdict banner and suite-status line are aria-live=polite; the preset group has a role=group with aria-label; results use th scope=row.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Validate as the user types and describe errors in text near the control, not colour alone.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The textarea re-parses on input; rejection reasons include the parse position and the exact Chromium behaviour in words, with colour only as reinforcement.

openQuestions.question: The JS model matches all published unit tests, but Chromium's net::structured_headers has more exotic corners (byte sequences with parameters, sf-token edge chars) that have no unit-test coverage in the DPO parser; if the upstream parser gains cases, this page's TESTS array should grow with them.

summary: A faithful, honestly-labelled re-implementation of Chromium's Performance-Observer header parser validated 9/9 against the shipped unit tests, demonstrating the void-vs-drop failure-mode split interactively.
